text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said Austria's neutrality and membership of NATO can be combined. However, no foreign troops or atomic weapons should be placed in Austria.
- Bank Austria chief Gerhard Randa plans to present the swap offers for the shareholders of Creditanstalt by early autumn.
- Bank Austria says a higher dividend for 1996 is possible as pre-tax profit rose seven percent to 5.2 billion schillings.
- Cartonboard makers Mayr-Melnhof and Alfred Wall AG have joined forces to build a cigarette packaging plant in Poland.
- An Austrian offer for industrial group IFE is favoured by Creditanstalt Investmentbank, which plans to sell its entire stake of 75 percent of the company.
DIE PRESSE
- Creditanstalt will not be merged with Bank Austria, which took over the bank at the beginning of the year, but a special joint committee is planned.
- Employees at papermaker Hallein Papier want to have talks with the management to try and stop the shedding of 150 jobs.
- Austrian Airlines' pre-tax profit jumped by 46.5 million schillings to 101.6 million schillings in 1996, but shareholders will receive no dividend.
KURIER

- President Thomas Klestil is against conservative ideas of changing the election modus for the president whereby the post would be elected by the national assembly. The president should be voted by the people.
- Bank Austria plans to cut 2,000 jobs in the next five years in Bank Austria and Creditanstalt.
- Bank Austria may create a special investment fund with Creditanstalt and Die Erste savings bank.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN

- Austria dismisses criticism over border control by Germany and expects to join the European Union's Schengen agreement in October. But calls for further army assistance on the European Union border are growing.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT

- Postal savings bank governor Erich Hampel, Bank Austria executive Heinrich Gehl, Creditanstalt executive Alarich Fenyves and Creditanstalt's leasing chief Ortwin Klapper are top candidates for becoming new board members of Creditanstalt.
OOE NACHRICHTEN
- 14 billion schillings are missing from the government's 1997 budget, threatening Austria's plan to join the European Economic and Monetary Union on time, the newspaper says.
